# The Talking Kettle Association

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

A member trying out smart glasses at Brew Break, our technology conference.

We are a membership organisation which supports blind and partially sighted people to use technology at home, at work and in education.

We have over 700 members across the UK and internationally, from people just starting out with technology to leading experts in assistive and accessible technology. Professionals and family members are welcome too, as associate members.

It is free to join, so there has never been a better time to get involved, learn more about technology and have a say in the future of the organisation.

## What can we help you with?

- [Get help with technology](https://tka.unremarkable.me/about-us/contact/)Email us or call our helpline, and we'll get back to you within 48 hours.
- [Free one-to-one training](https://tka.unremarkable.me/supporting-you/training/)Up to five hours, for work, volunteering or study.
- [Join for free](https://tka.unremarkable.me/membership/)Full membership if you are blind or partially sighted, associate membership if you support us.
- [Come to an event](https://tka.unremarkable.me/events/)Kettle Chat every month, masterclass webinars and Brew Break.
- [Find a service](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/)Our directory of organisations, trainers, suppliers and grants.

## Latest news

- Open Hands Technology Trust has become part of TKA 5 November 2026 "We have ambitious plans for the future," said Morgan Ashby, TKA Chair of Trustees. "The resources which are coming from OHTT will enable us to kick-start a number of new developments, and we are delighted to be able to build on OHTT's legacy."
- Masterclass Series: Using JAWS with Microsoft Office 26 October 2026 A new Masterclass Series introduces the JAWS screen reader with Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook. You can watch the recording of Session 1. Session 2 was on 4 November, and Session 3 is on 2 December.
- TKA welcomes a new team member 23 October 2026 Priya Lennox has joined us in the new role of Community Development Lead.

[All news](https://tka.unremarkable.me/news/)

# Supporting you

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/supporting-you/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

We provide advice, support and training for our members and for other blind and partially sighted people learning to use technology, and information for professionals and family members.

## Help when you're stuck

Email us at [hello@tka.unremarkable.me](mailto:hello@tka.unremarkable.me), or call our helpline on 020 7946 0321 and leave a message. We'll get back to you within 48 hours.

## Email discussion list

As a member, you can raise a technical question with our email discussion list, which includes a number of experts on mainstream and specialist technology.

## Kettle Chat

Members can join our friendly Kettle Chat on Zoom on the first Thursday of every month, from 7.30 to 9pm. We share updates on new technology and apps, and answer any questions you have. A member of our board hosts it.

## Masterclass webinars

Every other month, a masterclass looks in detail at accessibility in a particular product or piece of software. We have reviewed the latest braille displays, looked at audio editing techniques, explored the BlindShell Classic 2 mobile phone, and tried the latest AI apps. Recordings are in our [Resources](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/).

## Career Talks

We talk to blind and partially sighted people who have had careers in all kinds of fields: some in technology, and others where technology made their chosen work possible. Come and be inspired. Recordings are in our [Resources](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/).

## Brew Break, our technology conference

Brew Break is very popular with members: a chance to catch up on the latest technology, try products, and meet other members over a sociable weekend. We are working on an exciting programme for Brew Break 2027.

## Free one-to-one training

Up to five hours of free training, for work and volunteering, or for students aged 18 and over.

[Free one-to-one training](https://tka.unremarkable.me/supporting-you/training/)

## Equipment and funding

Advice on what to use, and where to find free equipment and grants to pay for it.

[Equipment and funding](https://tka.unremarkable.me/supporting-you/equipment-and-funding/)

## Coding and Computing Group

Our special interest group promotes accessibility in coding and computing. It encourages and supports young visually impaired people to study coding and computer science and to explore careers in them, and it promotes accessibility in coding tools and development environments.


---

# Free one-to-one training

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/supporting-you/training/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

Up to five hours of free one-to-one training, shaped around what you need to do.

## Technology for Work

For members getting ready for paid work, volunteering or work experience. It helps you gain the IT skills needed in the workplace so that, with other pre-employment support, you are ready to take the step.

1. **An assessment.** We find out the kind of work you are looking for and the IT skills you already have, and agree a learning plan.
2. **Setting up.** We suggest the software or hardware likely to help most. We can connect to your laptop or PC remotely to install and configure it, and tell you about trusted suppliers if you need to buy anything.
3. **Five one-hour sessions**, usually a week apart, to build skills and confidence, with tasks between sessions if they help.
4. **A follow-up** a few weeks later, for anything you still need help with, and our recommendations for learning on your own.

## Technology for Learning

For visually impaired students aged 18 and over, to build the skills you need for education and to prepare for the world of work.

Training can cover screen readers or magnification with Microsoft Outlook, Excel, Word and PowerPoint, Zoom and Teams, web browsers, and smartphones and their apps. We shape it around the skills you are likely to need, give you resources to keep learning afterwards, advise on equipment and software, can set up your PC remotely, and can tell you about grant-making trusts that may help pay for technology.

## Ask about training

Email [hello@tka.unremarkable.me](mailto:hello@tka.unremarkable.me), or call 020 7946 0321 and leave a message.

If you need advice on using technology, or on organisations that provide free equipment and grants for it, we can help.

Email [hello@tka.unremarkable.me](mailto:hello@tka.unremarkable.me), or call 020 7946 0321 and leave a message.

## Two schemes that have joined us

- **Open Hands Technology Trust (OHTT)** became part of TKA on 30 October 2026. Its device scheme has now closed.
- **The Ringing Bell Fund** is now run by TKA.

For either, contact us in the same way, and we'll help you find what you need.

Our [directory](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/) also lists organisations that give grants and equipment.

# Membership

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/membership/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

It is free to become a member, so there has never been a better time to get involved, learn more about technology and have a say in our future.

## Full and associate membership

- **Full membership** is for people who are blind or partially sighted. Full members elect the trustees who run the charity, and vote on proposals at the Annual General Meeting.
- **Associate membership** is for anyone else who supports our aims: professionals, family members and friends.

Together, members make sure everything we do is shaped by the experience of people with a visual impairment and of people working in the sector. They give the charity a powerful voice when we push for better products and services, and many share what they know through the discussion list, Kettle Chat and Brew Break.

## What every member gets

- Email updates on our webinars, events and technology news
- Contact with the charity at any time, by phone or email
- The email discussion list, where members ask questions and get informed, prompt answers
- Regular training events on Zoom, on topics members suggest
- One-to-one help at the monthly Kettle Chat
- Free one-to-one training, such as Technology for Work
- Discounts at Brew Break

## Join

In the finished site, a short form here lets you join as a full or associate member. In this preview, there is no form.

# Events

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/events/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

- Masterclass: Agentic Accessibility Webinar, Wednesday 25 November 2026, 7.30pm For decades, accessibility has largely meant making technology easier for blind and partially sighted people to operate. But what happens when we can simply tell an AI agent what we want to achieve, and let it do the work? Robin Hale, blind for 40 years and an assistive technology trainer for 15 of them, reports back from months of hands-on experiments with today's AI agents: what works, what doesn't, and what might come next.
- Masterclass Series: using JAWS with Word, Excel and Outlook Webinar, 21 October to 2 December 2026, 7.30pm
- Kettle Chat Webinar, the first Thursday of every month, 7.30pm, until July 2027 An informal conversation about technology, hosted by a trustee: help with problems, and talk about new products.

Webinar details are emailed to members. [Joining is free](https://tka.unremarkable.me/membership/).

# Shop

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/shop/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

Guide Hamsters for the Blind: five volumes of comic poems and performances, on CD and as audio downloads.

The series was the idea of one of our members, made possible by a folk poet who donated all the material and by many well-known voices who performed it. The first volume was launched in July 2003, and a new one every two years until 2011. Money from every copy helps us support blind and partially sighted people to use technology.

## The volumes

1. Guide Hamsters for the Blind
2. Missing Syrians
3. Top Hamster
4. Hamster Nav
5. Herding Hamsters

Each is available on CD or as an audio download, and all five come as a set.

In the finished site, each volume has a page with its tracks, a sample to listen to, and a way to buy it. In this preview, nothing is for sale.

# About us

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/about-us/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

The Talking Kettle Association (TKA) is a community of visually impaired people committed to improving access to mainstream and assistive technology.

We offer training, discussion, networking and help to anyone with a visual impairment.

## Since 1969

We were founded in 1969 as The British Typewriter Club for the Blind (BTCB), the oldest computer association for visually impaired people in the world. We changed our name in November 2018, to welcome people who are partially sighted as well as people who are blind.

## What we do

- We promote the use of computers and technology by visually impaired people.
- We encourage visually impaired people to explore what technology can do at home, at work and for leisure.
- We share advances in technology, and find the resources and information that matter.
- We encourage peer support among our members and among visually impaired people more widely.
- We campaign for equal access to computers, technology and the internet.
- We provide tutorials and training at every level of skill and interest.
- We create networking opportunities for visually impaired people in many sectors, and hold events for members.

## Who our members are

Everyone from people taking their first steps with technology to people working in the IT industry: people using technology for leisure, students at school or university, people using technology at work, developers, network architects and security specialists, researchers and academics, and organisations representing or building for visually impaired people. Our greatest asset is our members: with so much knowledge and experience among them, there is always someone who can help.

## Working in partnership

We work with other organisations in the sight loss sector. We are a partner of Sightlines Network, which represents many local sight loss charities across the UK, and we are part of the technology working group of The Sight Loss Alliance, which brings together the national sight loss charities.

## How we are run

We are a charitable company, incorporated in Scotland and regulated by the Scottish Charity Regulator, and we serve the whole of the UK. Our full members elect our trustees and vote at the Annual General Meeting. Our registered office is in Edinburgh, and our team works remotely.

In the finished site, this section links to the trustees and staff, the constitution, the report and accounts, safeguarding, complaints and the privacy policy.

## Contact us

[How to contact us](https://tka.unremarkable.me/about-us/contact/)

# Accessibility statement

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/accessibility/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

This site is built so that nobody, whether reading the screen, using assistive technology or sending an agent, loses access to anything on it.

It is built to [Zero Information Casualty version 1.7](https://zeroinformationcasualty.org/), and aims to meet WCAG 2.2 at level AA, with all text meeting AAA contrast.

## How it is built

- Every page is plain HTML. Nothing depends on JavaScript, and the site uses none.
- One main heading on every page, headings in order, landmarks, and a skip link to the main content.
- The logo is read once, as the charity's name.
- The font is Atkinson Hyperlegible, designed by the Braille Institute for readers with low vision.
- Every text colour meets 7:1 contrast. A dark scheme follows your system setting, and if your system asks for more contrast, secondary text and lines change to the full text colour.
- Text sizes are relative, so the site follows your browser's text size and zoom.
- Every picture is described, and nothing moves.
- The site sets no cookies, so there's no cookie banner.
- Every page has a Markdown version for agents, and the site has an llms.txt.

## What has been checked

- **9 November 2026, the home page, heard with NVDA 2026.3.1**, reading from top to bottom and moving through it with Tab, by someone who uses a screen reader every day. Headings, lists, landmarks, the drawing and its caption, and the order of the links were all as intended. Two problems were found, and both are fixed (below).
- **9 November 2026:** the build checks that no placeholder is left unfilled, and every text colour was measured.

## Not yet checked

- Listening to every other kind of page with a screen reader: the inside pages, the directory and its entries. The results will be written here with dates.
- VoiceOver on iPhone and Mac.
- Phone widths with text enlarged.
- Windows High Contrast.

## Found and fixed

- **9 November 2026: a link to the page you were on.** In the menu, the current page was a link to itself, so NVDA said "same page link, current page, Home". It is now named as the current page, but is no longer a link.
- **9 November 2026: "Preview" said twice.** The preview note was a landmark named Preview that began with the word Preview, so NVDA read the word twice. It is now a plain note.

## Known issues

None known. Only the home page has been heard so far, so this site makes no claim about the other pages beyond how they are built.

## Reporting a problem

Every page ends with "Fix something on this page", which opens a short form that already knows which page you were on. It doesn't ask who you are.

# Learn to use technology

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/learn/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

44 entries, A to Z.

- [AAT Solutions: Expert Assistive Technology Training](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/aat-solutions-expert-assistive-technology-training/) At AAT Solutions, we specialize in helping visually impaired individuals use assistive technology confidently and effectively.
- [AbilityNet](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/abilitynet-information-and-advice/) AbilityNet is a UK-based charity with a global reach - our vision is a digital world accessible to all.
- [Access On](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/access-on/) Access On is the technology podcast of the National Federation of the Blind in the US and is hosted by Jonathan Mosen.
- [Access Tech VIP](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/access-tech-vip/) Access Tech VIP is led by Adrian Tamasan, a blind assistive technology trainer with more than 25 years of experience using screen readers across Windows, macOS, iOS, Android and specialist audio workflows.
- [Accessible Android](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/accessible-android/) This website provides tips, how to guides, app reviews and podcasts on using Android on smartphones and tablets with the Talkback screen reader, Braille displays and other accessibility features.
- [AFB (American Foundation for the Blind): Access World](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/afb-american-foundation-for-the-blind-access-world/) Produced by American Foundation for the Blind, Access World is &quot;a trusted source of information for the intersection of disability and technology.
- [Alternate Visions Coaching (AVC)](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/alternate-visions-coaching-avc/) AVC specialise in sight loss, assistive technology training, coaching for living with sight loss, back to work skills &amp; confidence building.
- [Apple Accessibility Pages](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/apple-accessibility-pages/) The Apple website has a really helpful section on accessibility features for people with little or no sight.
- [Apple Accessibility YouTube Channel](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/apple-accessibility-you-tube-channel/) This collection of videos looks at using your iPhone without seeing the screen, adapting gestures to your physical needs, and more.
- [AppleVis](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/applevis/) AppleVis is the go-to resource for blind and low vision users of Apple technologies.
- [Aspire Consultancy](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/aspire-consultancy/) Aspire Consultancy is an independent company that provides quality advice, assessment and a training service on all aspects of assistive technology for visually impaired people.
- [Azabat Touch Typing Software](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/azabat-touch-typing-software/) The Azabat Touch Typing Tutors are software programmes designed specifically to help blind and partially sighted people to learn to touch type.
- [Blind Android Users](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/blind-android-users/) The team at Blind Android Users strive to make Android understandable, thus demystifying the claim by some who continue to perpetuate the myth among unsuspecting blind folks that Android isn’t usable by the blind.
- [BrailleCast podcast: Connecting the Dots](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/braillecast-podcast-connecting-the-dots/) The BrailleCast podcast aims to showcase the value of Braille and provide Braillists with resources to help spread the word about Braille.
- [Computer Room Services](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/computer-room-services/) We offer training on all the main screen reading packages and also on a wide variety of software including WordPress.
- [Dolphin Computer Access](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/dolphin-computer-access/) Dolphin assistive technology products are designed to improve accessibility and independence on computers, smartphones and tablets for people with a wide range of vision impairments.
- [Doorway Online Touch Typing website](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/doorway-online-touch-typing-website/) Doorway will take you from your first lesson, using the home keys right through to the most advanced level.
- [Double Tap](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/double-tap-on-air/) This is presented by Stephen Scott and Shaun Preece, formerly of RNIB Tech Talk.
- [Eyes on Success: Assistive Technology Podcast](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/eyes-on-success-assistive-technology-podcast/) Eyes On Success is a weekly podcast and radio program dedicated to empowering the visually impaired community.
- [Facebook Group: JAWS Screen Reader Users](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/facebook-group-jaws-screen-reader-users/) This group is for the discussion of the Jaws screen reader.
- [Facebook Group: NVDA screen reader users](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/facebook-nvda-screen-reader-users/) This group provides NVDA users different things, add-ons, NVDA versions, discussions, and sharing opinions.
- [Freedom Scientific Training Podcast](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/freedom-scientific-training-podcast/) Would you like to download Freedom Scientific’s audio training content on your smart phone or mobile device?
- [Gary Eady Computer Training](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/gary-eady-computer-training/) Gary has more than 25 years knowledge and experience at working with blind and partially sighted people.
- [Hartgen Consultancy](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/hartgen-consultancy/) At Hartgen Consultancy we believe in providing visually impaired people with the best possible service and support.
- [Henshaws: Knowledge Village - Assistive Technology](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/henshaws-knowledge-village-assistive-technology/) Assistive Technology is a game changer for people with sight loss and, with the right training and practice, can restore independence.
- [Humanware](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/humanware/) For over 30 years, HumanWare’s inspirational vision has resulted in a range of highly intuitive and intelligent solutions that empower people who are blind or with low vision by giving them the independence to participate effectively within a sighted world.
- [In Touch on BBC Radio 4](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/in-touch-on-bbc-radio-4/) The BBC programme In Touch provides news, views and information for people who are blind or partially sighted, and includes features on technology.
- [Justin Macleod](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/justin-macleod/) I have taught students in the areas of audio restoration; mixing; basic mastering, audio fundamentals and concepts; electronic music production; dialogue editing; and sound design.
- [Macaccessibility Roundtable podcast](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/macaccessibility-roundtable-podcast/) The Maccessibility website and podcast is devoted to connecting and providing easy access to the best resources for blind, visually impaired, and other disability groups using Apple products.
- [Microsoft Accessibility Tools for Vision](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/microsoft-accessibility-tools-for-vision/) This page lists sight-related accessibility tools to help all Microsoft Windows and Microsoft 365 users.
- [Mystic Access](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/mystic-access/) Mystic Access provides online audio documentation and tutorials for purchase on accessible products, software and services for the blind and visually impaired.
- [National Braille Press: Computers &amp; Technology](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/national-braille-press-computers-technology/) The National Braille Press is in the USA and which, despite its name, produces books in Braille, eBraille, DAISY, a navigable audio format and MS Word.
- [NatSIP Advisors](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/natsip-directory/) NatSIP, the National Sensory Impairment Partnership is a partnership of organisations working together to improve outcomes for children and young people with sensory impairment.
- [Personaleyes](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/personaleyes/) Davinder Kullar from Personaleyes offers tailored training, support and coaching to blind and partially sighted people on a range of technology, such as computers, smart phones, tablets through to smart speakers and everyday living solutions.
- [RNIB: Digital Skills Team](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/rnib-technology-for-life-team/) RNIB's Digital Skills team can help with all kinds of requests including information, advice and guidance over the phone, over email or with a volunteer.
- [RNIB: Tech Talk Podcast](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/rnib-tech-talk-podcast/) Tech Talk is a podcast and radio show for blind and partially sighted people who are interested in accessible technology.
- [RNIB: Technology for Independent Learning](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/rnib-technology-for-independent-learning/) The RNIB provide an overview of the role of technology in the development of a child or young person, the role of the QTVI (Qualified Teachers of children and young people with Vision Impairment), and provide information on some the mainstream and specialist solutions which are available.
- [Sight &amp; Sound Technology](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/sight-sound-technology/) Sight and Sound Technology is an accredited training provider with resources across the UK and Ireland.
- [Sight for Surrey Technology Training Resources](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/sight-for-surry-technology-training-resources/) Please find below a link which takes you to the ICT Handouts and Tutorials page of the Sight For Surrey website.
- [Taira Technology](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/taira-technology/) Taira Technology is a family run business that helps blind and visually impaired individuals and organisations with every aspect of technology.
- [Talking Technology with VI Labs](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/talking-technology-with-vi-labs/) This podcast focuses on technology that supports people who are blind and visually impaired.
- [Tech Selector - hosted by Guide Dogs](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/tech-selector-hosted-by-guide-dogs/) Technology is a huge part of our everyday lives.
- [Tek Talk by Accessible World](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/tek-talk-by-accessible-world/) For well over 20 years, Tek Talk has hosted weekly audio presentations on new software, products and tools for blind and visually impaired people across the world.
- [Thomas Pocklington Trust: Education Technology](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/thomas-pocklington-trust-education-technology/) Whether you’re at school, college or university, technology plays a vital role in your education.

- [Computer Room Services](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/computer-room-services/) We offer training on all the main screen reading packages and also on a wide variety of software including WordPress.
- [Dolphin Computer Access](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/dolphin-computer-access/) Dolphin assistive technology products are designed to improve accessibility and independence on computers, smartphones and tablets for people with a wide range of vision impairments.
- [Humanware](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/humanware/) For over 30 years, HumanWare’s inspirational vision has resulted in a range of highly intuitive and intelligent solutions that empower people who are blind or with low vision by giving them the independence to participate effectively within a sighted world.
- [Optelec](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/optelec/) We are one of the UK’s largest and leaders in manufacturing Low Vision Technology for all areas of sight loss.
- [Pamtrad UK](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/pamtrad-uk/) Pamtrad UK are a provider of a wide range of specialist equipment, from electronic magnifiers and text to speech systems to computer access software.
- [Professional Vision Services](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/professional-vision-services/) Professional Vision Services was incorporated in 1990 by Philippa Wisbey - Managing Director and owner, importing the Magnilink brand of video magnifiers and reading machines from Low Vision International (LVI) into the UK.
- [Ray-Ban Meta Glasses](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/rayban/) Useful links:
- [RNIB: Digital Skills Team](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/rnib-technology-for-life-team/) RNIB's Digital Skills team can help with all kinds of requests including information, advice and guidance over the phone, over email or with a volunteer.

- [Blind Aid](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/blind-aid/) Living with blindness or visual impairment brings many challenges to everyday life.

- [The Powell Family Foundation (TPFF)](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/powell-family-foundation/) The aim of The Powell Family Foundation is to support vision impaired children, young people and adults aged 25 and under, to improve their emotional and physical well-being, increase their knowledge and skills, and support their independence through the provision of grants to individuals and charitable organisations.
- [VICTA grant scheme for children and young adults](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/victa-grant-scheme-for-children-and-young-adults/) For visually impaired children and young people aged 8 to 29, VICTA can provide grants for laptops, software and items for independent living for home use.

- [Access On](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/access-on/) Access On is the technology podcast of the National Federation of the Blind in the US and is hosted by Jonathan Mosen.
- [Accessible Android](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/accessible-android/) This website provides tips, how to guides, app reviews and podcasts on using Android on smartphones and tablets with the Talkback screen reader, Braille displays and other accessibility features.
- [AFB (American Foundation for the Blind): Access World](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/afb-american-foundation-for-the-blind-access-world/) Produced by American Foundation for the Blind, Access World is &quot;a trusted source of information for the intersection of disability and technology.
- [Apple Accessibility Pages](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/apple-accessibility-pages/) The Apple website has a really helpful section on accessibility features for people with little or no sight.
- [Apple Accessibility YouTube Channel](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/apple-accessibility-you-tube-channel/) This collection of videos looks at using your iPhone without seeing the screen, adapting gestures to your physical needs, and more.
- [AppleVis](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/applevis/) AppleVis is the go-to resource for blind and low vision users of Apple technologies.
- [Blind Android Users](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/blind-android-users/) The team at Blind Android Users strive to make Android understandable, thus demystifying the claim by some who continue to perpetuate the myth among unsuspecting blind folks that Android isn’t usable by the blind.
- [BrailleCast podcast: Connecting the Dots](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/braillecast-podcast-connecting-the-dots/) The BrailleCast podcast aims to showcase the value of Braille and provide Braillists with resources to help spread the word about Braille.
- [Double Tap](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/double-tap-on-air/) This is presented by Stephen Scott and Shaun Preece, formerly of RNIB Tech Talk.
- [Eyes on Success: Assistive Technology Podcast](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/eyes-on-success-assistive-technology-podcast/) Eyes On Success is a weekly podcast and radio program dedicated to empowering the visually impaired community.
- [Facebook Group: JAWS Screen Reader Users](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/facebook-group-jaws-screen-reader-users/) This group is for the discussion of the Jaws screen reader.
- [Facebook Group: NVDA screen reader users](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/facebook-nvda-screen-reader-users/) This group provides NVDA users different things, add-ons, NVDA versions, discussions, and sharing opinions.
- [Freedom Scientific Training Podcast](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/freedom-scientific-training-podcast/) Would you like to download Freedom Scientific’s audio training content on your smart phone or mobile device?
- [Henshaws: Knowledge Village - Assistive Technology](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/henshaws-knowledge-village-assistive-technology/) Assistive Technology is a game changer for people with sight loss and, with the right training and practice, can restore independence.
- [In Touch on BBC Radio 4](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/in-touch-on-bbc-radio-4/) The BBC programme In Touch provides news, views and information for people who are blind or partially sighted, and includes features on technology.
- [Macaccessibility Roundtable podcast](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/macaccessibility-roundtable-podcast/) The Maccessibility website and podcast is devoted to connecting and providing easy access to the best resources for blind, visually impaired, and other disability groups using Apple products.
- [Microsoft Accessibility Tools for Vision](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/microsoft-accessibility-tools-for-vision/) This page lists sight-related accessibility tools to help all Microsoft Windows and Microsoft 365 users.
- [Mystic Access](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/mystic-access/) Mystic Access provides online audio documentation and tutorials for purchase on accessible products, software and services for the blind and visually impaired.
- [National Braille Press: Computers &amp; Technology](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/national-braille-press-computers-technology/) The National Braille Press is in the USA and which, despite its name, produces books in Braille, eBraille, DAISY, a navigable audio format and MS Word.
- [RNIB: Digital Skills Team](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/rnib-technology-for-life-team/) RNIB's Digital Skills team can help with all kinds of requests including information, advice and guidance over the phone, over email or with a volunteer.
- [RNIB: Tech Talk Podcast](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/rnib-tech-talk-podcast/) Tech Talk is a podcast and radio show for blind and partially sighted people who are interested in accessible technology.
- [RNIB: Technology for Independent Learning](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/rnib-technology-for-independent-learning/) The RNIB provide an overview of the role of technology in the development of a child or young person, the role of the QTVI (Qualified Teachers of children and young people with Vision Impairment), and provide information on some the mainstream and specialist solutions which are available.
- [Sight for Surrey Technology Training Resources](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/sight-for-surry-technology-training-resources/) Please find below a link which takes you to the ICT Handouts and Tutorials page of the Sight For Surrey website.
- [Talking Technology with VI Labs](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/talking-technology-with-vi-labs/) This podcast focuses on technology that supports people who are blind and visually impaired.
- [Tech Selector - hosted by Guide Dogs](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/tech-selector-hosted-by-guide-dogs/) Technology is a huge part of our everyday lives.
- [Tek Talk by Accessible World](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/tek-talk-by-accessible-world/) For well over 20 years, Tek Talk has hosted weekly audio presentations on new software, products and tools for blind and visually impaired people across the world.
- [Thomas Pocklington Trust: Education Technology](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/thomas-pocklington-trust-education-technology/) Whether you’re at school, college or university, technology plays a vital role in your education.

## Products

2 entries

- [Ray-Ban Meta Glasses](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/rayban/) Useful links:
- [Visably](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/visably/) This charity (previously known as British Wireless for the Blind Fund) provides audio devices, radios and audiobook players to visually impaired adults and children for free.

## Professional bodies

2 entries

- [DATEurope](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/dateurope/) DATEurope is the recently founded European Industry Association for Digital Assistive Technology.
- [UKAAF (UK Association for Accessible Formats)](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/ukaaf-uk-association-for-accessible-formats/) TKA is a Sponsoring Member of UKAAF, the industry association that sets standards and promotes best practice for accessible documents in the UK.

## Research

6 entries

- [Connect to Success: Technology and Employment Support for Disabled People](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/connect-to-success-technology-and-employment-support-for-disabled-people/) The Government should improve employment opportunities for disabled jobseekers by taking advantage of modern assistive and accessible technology.
- [Employment Facts and Stats 2020 Report](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/employment-facts-and-stats-2020-report/) This document by RNIB sets out the key facts, stats and trends on the employment situation of blind and partially sighted people.
- [ENABLER Project: Tackling unemployment for blind and partially sighted people](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/enabler-project-tackling-unemployment-for-blind-and-partially-sighted-people/) Executive summary
- [See My Skills: Breaking the cycle of unemployment for blind and partially sighted people](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/see-my-skills-breaking-the-cycle-of-unemployment-for-blind-and-partially-sighted-people/) This report by The Vision Foundation sets out a roadmap to ensure that everyone, sighted or blind, has the chance to enjoy the independence, purpose and meaning that employment can bring.
- [Sight Loss and Technology Briefing Report, 2024](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/sight-loss-and-technology-briefing-report-2024/) This briefing has been produced and published on behalf of the technology group of The Sight Loss Alliance, which TKA is part of.
- [Talent and Technology Report](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/talent-and-technology-report/) The report was produced by Policy Connect on behalf of the The All-Party Parliamentary Group for Assistive Technology.

## Retailers

10 entries

- [Aspire Consultancy](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/aspire-consultancy/) Aspire Consultancy is an independent company that provides quality advice, assessment and a training service on all aspects of assistive technology for visually impaired people.
- [Computer Room Services](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/computer-room-services/) We offer training on all the main screen reading packages and also on a wide variety of software including WordPress.
- [Dolphin Computer Access](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/dolphin-computer-access/) Dolphin assistive technology products are designed to improve accessibility and independence on computers, smartphones and tablets for people with a wide range of vision impairments.
- [Humanware](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/humanware/) For over 30 years, HumanWare’s inspirational vision has resulted in a range of highly intuitive and intelligent solutions that empower people who are blind or with low vision by giving them the independence to participate effectively within a sighted world.
- [Optelec](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/optelec/) We are one of the UK’s largest and leaders in manufacturing Low Vision Technology for all areas of sight loss.
- [Pamtrad UK](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/pamtrad-uk/) Pamtrad UK are a provider of a wide range of specialist equipment, from electronic magnifiers and text to speech systems to computer access software.
- [Professional Vision Services](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/professional-vision-services/) Professional Vision Services was incorporated in 1990 by Philippa Wisbey - Managing Director and owner, importing the Magnilink brand of video magnifiers and reading machines from Low Vision International (LVI) into the UK.
- [RNIB: Digital Skills Team](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/rnib-technology-for-life-team/) RNIB's Digital Skills team can help with all kinds of requests including information, advice and guidance over the phone, over email or with a volunteer.
- [Sight &amp; Sound Technology](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/sight-sound-technology/) Sight and Sound Technology is an accredited training provider with resources across the UK and Ireland.
- [VisionAid Technologies](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/visionaid-technologies/) VisionAid Technologies Ltd is a family owned &amp; run business who have been providing solutions to assist partially sighted &amp; blind people since 1996.

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

- [Sight City](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/sight-city/) SightCity Frankfurt claims to be the world’s largest trade fair for aids and solutions for the blind and visually impaired.
- [Sight for Surrey Technology Training Resources](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/sight-for-surry-technology-training-resources/) Please find below a link which takes you to the ICT Handouts and Tutorials page of the Sight For Surrey website.
- [Sight Loss and Technology Briefing Report, 2024](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/sight-loss-and-technology-briefing-report-2024/) This briefing has been produced and published on behalf of the technology group of The Sight Loss Alliance, which TKA is part of.
- [Sight Tech Global](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/sight-tech-global/) Sight Tech Global is a world-wide, virtual conference dedicated to highlighting technology's power to transform lives for people living with vision loss around the world by bringing together the pioneers who are applying the latest technology advances to barrier-free navigation, human interaction, and low-friction access to information for people who are blind or visually impaired.
- [Sight Village](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/sight-village/) Sight Village is described as 'the UK’s leading exhibition for blind and partially sighted people and for those experiencing sight problems’.
- [Sound Without Sight](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/sound-without-sight/) Sound Without Sight is a new non-profit initiative, aimed at supporting sight-impaired people in the fields of audio and music.
- [Taira Technology](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/taira-technology/) Taira Technology is a family run business that helps blind and visually impaired individuals and organisations with every aspect of technology.
- [Talent and Technology Report](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/talent-and-technology-report/) The report was produced by Policy Connect on behalf of the The All-Party Parliamentary Group for Assistive Technology.
- [Talking Technology with VI Labs](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/talking-technology-with-vi-labs/) This podcast focuses on technology that supports people who are blind and visually impaired.
- [Tech Selector - hosted by Guide Dogs](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/tech-selector-hosted-by-guide-dogs/) Technology is a huge part of our everyday lives.
- [TechShare Pro](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/techshare-pro/) AbilityNet’s annual TechShare Pro conference gathers the community of people who are creating a digital world accessible to all:
- [Tek Talk by Accessible World](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/tek-talk-by-accessible-world/) For well over 20 years, Tek Talk has hosted weekly audio presentations on new software, products and tools for blind and visually impaired people across the world.
- [The Powell Family Foundation (TPFF)](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/powell-family-foundation/) The aim of The Powell Family Foundation is to support vision impaired children, young people and adults aged 25 and under, to improve their emotional and physical well-being, increase their knowledge and skills, and support their independence through the provision of grants to individuals and charitable organisations.
- [Thomas Pocklington Trust: Education Technology](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/thomas-pocklington-trust-education-technology/) Whether you’re at school, college or university, technology plays a vital role in your education.
- [TripleTapTech](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/tripletaptech/) TripleTapTech is a dedicated resource for individuals with visual impairments, providing expert advice, support, and training on all things technology.
- [UKAAF (UK Association for Accessible Formats)](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/ukaaf-uk-association-for-accessible-formats/) TKA is a Sponsoring Member of UKAAF, the industry association that sets standards and promotes best practice for accessible documents in the UK.
- [VICTA grant scheme for children and young adults](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/victa-grant-scheme-for-children-and-young-adults/) For visually impaired children and young people aged 8 to 29, VICTA can provide grants for laptops, software and items for independent living for home use.
- [Visably](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/visably/) This charity (previously known as British Wireless for the Blind Fund) provides audio devices, radios and audiobook players to visually impaired adults and children for free.
- [VisionAid Technologies](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/visionaid-technologies/) VisionAid Technologies Ltd is a family owned &amp; run business who have been providing solutions to assist partially sighted &amp; blind people since 1996.

# AAT Solutions: Expert Assistive Technology Training

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/aat-solutions-expert-assistive-technology-training/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

At AAT Solutions, we specialize in helping visually impaired individuals use assistive technology confidently and effectively. As a certified trainer who is blind, I bring a unique perspective and personal experience that greatly enhance our training.

Personalized Training: We offer training sessions tailored to your needs. Our focus includes key tools like JAWS, NVDA, ZoomText, and Dragon NaturallySpeaking. We make sure you can use these tools easily in your everyday life, whether at home or work.

Unique Advantage: My personal experience as a blind individual helps me understand the real challenges of using assistive technology. This allows me to offer practical and empathetic support, helping you overcome obstacles and build confidence with tailored strategies.

Broad Device Training: Besides assistive technologies, we also provide training on popular platforms like Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android. This helps you become comfortable with various types of technology, improving your overall digital skills and readiness.

Hands-On Learning: Our sessions focus on practical, hands-on learning. You’ll practice using your new skills in real-life situations, making it easier to apply what you’ve learned effectively.

Ongoing Support: We are dedicated to your success. We offer continuous support and encouragement, helping you build confidence and address any challenges you may face as you use your new skills.

AbilityNet is a UK-based charity with a global reach - our vision is a digital world accessible to all.

We’ve been helping older people and disabled people of any age with their technology for 25 years. Could we help you or someone you know?

- We have a network of more than 450 friendly tech volunteers who can help you or someone you are supporting. They can come to your home, or help you on the phone.

- If you are older or disabled, or if you support someone that is, you can call our helpline for independent advice from a technology expert.

# Alternate Visions Coaching (AVC)

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/alternate-visions-coaching-avc/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

AVC specialise in sight loss, assistive technology training, coaching for living with sight loss, back to work skills &amp; confidence building.

AVC specialises in delivering training on VoiceOver for Apple products. VoiceOver is a built-in screen reader found on all modern Apple devices. It gives Apple users full accessibility to all of the features of their device, without the need to purchase additional software.

AVC also offers training to users of Dolphin GuideConnect and Dolphin SuperNova. These are software packages that can be installed on most modern Windows 10 tablets, Desktop and Laptop computers. They enable visually impaired and blind individuals to use computers by utilising magnification, colour contrast, screen reading software or in some cases, a combination of all of those features.

Training in the use of these assistive technologies can be delivered to individuals or groups and is tailored to your individual needs. Training can be given in the comfort of the client’s own home on their own device, or if the client is a company/organisation, it can be delivered on their premises.

AVC understands that individuals may feel uncomfortable receiving strangers into their home, so offers remote training by telephone or video calling services as an alternative.

## Contact

- Website: [alternatevisionscoaching.org](http://alternatevisionscoaching.org)
- Email: [alternatevisionscoaching@gmail.com](mailto:alternatevisionscoaching@gmail.com)
- Phone: 07801 446624

# Blatchington Court Trust: Grant Guidelines

Applications will be considered for children and young people who are registered or are registrable as blind (SSI) or partially sighted (SI) up to and including the age of 29 years and who reside permanently in Sussex. All items supplied through our grant scheme are for home use only (not for school or college), unless there has been a special arrangement between the Trust and the local Authority’s teams of qualified Teachers for Visual Impairment (QTVI’s).All applications must be supported by a QTVI or another professional if the applicant is over 16.

# Blind Aid

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/blind-aid/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

Living with blindness or visual impairment brings many challenges to everyday life.

Grants are available to visually impaired Londoners on low incomes for essential items to help maintain vital independence.

BlindAid grants are:

-

Subject to criteria, and considered by our grant committee

- Typically up to £400

- Applied for on behalf of the recipient by Social Services, Sensory Teams or other Charities/statutory services.

Grants can be used in many ways, including but not limited to:

- Equipment and gadgets, including colour detectors, talking microwaves etc.

- White Goods

- Accessible computers/laptops

- Domestic items

Please be aware that we can only accept grant applications made by an employee of a statutory organisation or registered charity.

The team at Blind Android Users strive to make Android understandable, thus demystifying the claim by some who continue to perpetuate the myth among unsuspecting blind folks that Android isn’t usable by the blind.

For this reason, Blind Android Users exists to set the record straight and provide tutorials (in both audio form) via our weekly podcast where we go through what Android is all about and how to use it as a blind or visually impaired person.

Android is the world’s biggest mobile platform and at Blind Android Users, we intend to make it possible for blind and visually impaired people to fully take advantage of the platform.

# Code Jumper

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/code-jumper/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

Code Jumper™ is an incredible innovation that teaches students who are blind or visually impaired computer coding. By putting the block code tactually in your hands, all students can learn together in an inclusive setting. Originally designed by Microsoft® and developed by APH, this educational toy bridges the skills gap and opens up the world of coding to every student.

Children not only learn basic programming concepts, such as sequence, iteration, selection, and variables, but will also be encouraged to think computationally, such as solving the same challenge in multiple ways.

Most important, any teacher can facilitate Code Jumper lessons without prior computer science experience, and Code Jumper is inclusive of all children across the vision spectrum.

APH is pleased to announce that we will be partnering with HumanWare to distribute Code Jumper internationally. HumanWare is a leader in assistive technology, with over 30 years of experience in empowering people who are blind or with low vision through innovative solutions.

We are also pleased to partner with the following organizations in the promotion and sale of Code Jumper internationally:

- Australia: Vision Australia Vision Australia: Vision Australia is a not-for-profit organisation, recognised as a leading national provider of blindness and low vision products and services in Australia. To purchase Code Jumper, please visit: Vision Store

- Canada: CNIB Foundation: CNIB

- UK: The Royal National Institute of Blind People (RNIB) – RNIB is one of the UK′s leading sight loss charities and the largest community of blind and partially sighted people. To purchase Code Jumper, please visit their online shop.

## Contact

- Website: [codejumper.com](https://codejumper.com/)

- [Work or study in technology](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/work/)

# Computer Room Services

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/computer-room-services/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

We offer training on all the main screen reading packages and also on a wide variety of software including WordPress.

We do not run specific courses, instead we try to tailor the training to your needs. Training can be done over the telephone or over Zoom or Microsoft Teams and can also be recorded for you to keep.

We train by the hour, a minimum of one hour must be taken, and then notes are emailed or sent in your preferred format at the end of the lesson. There are no contracts – you can take as few or as many lessons as you wish. Home visits can be arranged.

We are also able to remotely connect to your PC, so that we can see, and show you, exactly what to do when training.

## Contact

- Website: [comproom.co.uk](http://www.comproom.co.uk)

# Connect to Success: Technology and Employment Support for Disabled People

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/connect-to-success-technology-and-employment-support-for-disabled-people/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

The Government should improve employment opportunities for disabled jobseekers by taking advantage of modern assistive and accessible technology.

Cross-party think tank Policy Connect and the All-Party Parliamentary Group for Assistive and Accessible Technology’s latest report, ‘Connect to Success: Technology and Employment Support for Disabled People’, examines the contribution of employment support services for disabled job seekers, and shows how these services can become more effective by providing support for their clients to use assistive and accessible technology (ATech) to overcome barriers to employment.

Rates of economic inactivity have proved persistently higher among disabled and neurodivergent people, with only 54.4% of working age disabled people in employment compared to 81.9% of non-disabled people. The situation is particularly acute for people with learning disabilities, with employment rates that are estimated to be between 4.8% and 26.7%.

The Get Britain Working White Paper has outlined the new Government’s plans to increase economic activity, with a long-term target of an 80% employment rate and 2.1 million more people in work. This can only be achieved if more disabled people are able to find and thrive in employment.

The report argues that government’s employment support reforms – including the creation of the ‘Connect to Work’ scheme that will support an estimated 100,000 disabled people over 2026-27 – offer a once-in-a generation opportunity to incorporate ATech into the design of these new and reformed services.

ATech is already a valued and common form of workplace adjustment, and as Connect to Success outlines, employment support services will prove most effective at breaking down barriers to work if they build access to ATech into their programmes for developing disabled clients’ employability skills and confidence.

Connect to Success sets out three recommendations for the Government to improve access to employment for disabled jobseekers by incorporating ATech into employment services:

- ATech should be part of the everyday delivery of the new jobs and careers service and be incorporated into local Get Britain Working Plans, including local Connect to Work schemes. Employment support clients should be helped to explore what ATech is right for them and begin using the technology, gaining skills and confidence with it, even before they secure paid work.

- Government should partner with the tech and disability sectors to establish a national Centre for ATech, whose role would include (i) providing strategic guidance to employment support service leaders and (ii) upskilling frontline professionals.

- Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) and post-16 essential skills provision should recognise ATech as a core employability and life skill for disabled people. ATech should be incorporated in all relevant standards and frameworks related to preparation for adulthood (PfA) SEND provision, and within any proposed National Standards for Personal, Social and Employability Qualifications.

“Connect to Success is a vital and timely contribution to ongoing discussions about employment and the need to ensure more people can enter and thrive in work. The report convincingly outlines the case for reforming employment support services with greater incorporation of technology to break down persistent barriers to employment for disabled people. Assistive and accessible technology (ATech) is already a valued and common form of workplace adjustment, and I hope very much the Government will seize the opportunity of its new Connect to Work scheme to expand access to this technology. By reducing barriers to accessing ATech and developing skills and confidence in its use, employment support services will be better placed to help their disabled clients secure paid work and build successful careers. It’s fantastic that Sir Stephen has made time during the Parliamentary Recess to address this launch event, and I look forward to working with colleagues in Parliament and the wider sector to help ensure ATech becomes an integral part of employment support delivery.” – Lord Shinkwin, All-Party Parliamentary Group for Assistive and Accessible Technology (APPGAT).

Download (docx 384.31 KB)

# Employment Facts and Stats 2020 Report

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/employment-facts-and-stats-2020-report/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

This document by RNIB sets out the key facts, stats and trends on the employment situation of blind and partially sighted people.

Some of the key findings include:

There is a significant employment gap between blind and partially sighted people and the general population. The employment rate is 76% in the general population, 51% amongst the disabled population excluding sight loss and 27% for people registered blind and partially sighted.

Several factors influence the likelihood of being in work: age; educational attainment; severity of sight loss; additional disabilities and general health.

Registered blind and partially sighted people with a degree or higher still only have the same chance of getting a job as someone with no qualifications in the general public.

The age at which someone experiences sight loss influences the challenges they face, either in entry to the job market or job retention. People born blind or who lost their sight in childhood are less likely to ever enter the labour market, with 76% of this group ever having a job compared to 96% of people who lost their sight over the age of 30. However, it is very likely other factors influence this such as additional disabilities.

Published 2020.

# ENABLER Project: Tackling unemployment for blind and partially sighted people

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/enabler-project-tackling-unemployment-for-blind-and-partially-sighted-people/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

Executive summary

What we did

Between 2010 and 2013, RNIB and the University of Birmingham carried out a three-year, action-based research project to help improve the employment prospects of blind and partially sighted people. Working alongside a group of employment specialists and approximately 100 blind and partially sighted people, we designed and tested:

• a standard assessment model that has increased our understanding of

the skills, aspirations and barriers to employment of blind and partially

sighted people

• innovative support strategies for those furthest from the labour market, which has helped inform how we deliver services for blind and partially sighted people seeking work.

Why we did it

Blind and partially sighted people are significantly less likely to be in paid employment than the general population or other disabled people. Only one in three registered blind and partially sighted people of working age is in paid employment. They are nearly five times more likely than the general population to have had no paid work for five years.

Blind and partially sighted people need specialist support on their journey towards employment. In addition to more common barriers, such as long term unemployment or low literacy and numeracy levels, blind and partially sighted job seekers have specific needs related to their sight loss.

What we found

We identified key factors that determine a blind or partially sighted person’s distance from the labour market, and whether they are ready for work.

Examples of those factors include:

• being able to self-advocate to employers, explaining what workplace adjustments will be required to carry out particular roles

• confidence and competence using computers adapted with appropriate assistive technology software

• confidence and ability to travel independently using public transport

• access to information via a preferred format of braille, large print, audio or electronic information.

We have shown that blind and partially sighted people furthest from the labour market require intensive support and specialist interventions in key areas.

These include:

• developing assistive technology skills

• developing mobility skills

• skills to communicate needs and associated adjustments to employers

• making the most of residual vision

• a pre-employment programme, designed to meet the complex needs of blind

and partially sighted people.

What we produced

We have developed a comprehensive employment assessment toolkit that takes account of the specific needs of blind and partially sighted job seekers.

It supports employment advisers and their clients to design interventions that help blind and partially sighted people on their path towards employment.

The employment assessment toolkit enables employment advisers, who work with blind and partially sighted people to gain a clear understanding of their clients’ aspirations in relation to employment, and what types of support and development are required. It can be used by any provider working in the welfare to work industry that supports blind and partially sighted people.

Trials of the employment assessment toolkit and innovative support strategies provided evidence of the effectiveness of a holistic and specialist employment service for people with sight loss. The toolkit was proven to be an important part of such a service and helps employment advisors, clients and managers to:

• establish a profile of each client’s particular skills and barriers

• identify and design effective interventions which are sensitive to the complex needs and circumstances of people with sight loss

• plan a tailored pre-employment programme

• establish a baseline, which can be compared with a reassessment following intervention

• record evidence of measurable success towards paid employment

• acknowledge and celebrate other meaningful outcomes such as greater independence, or contribution and participation through voluntary work

• gather information about the range and number of clients being supported at different levels of need.

The new employment assessment toolkit is helping the RNIB group of charities to re-model the way it delivers pre-employment support with blind and partially sighted people. Designed to assess the particular issues faced by blind and partially sighted people, it serves as a diagnostic tool and is useful for planning the steps required to progress towards work. The RNIB group of charities is embedding the employment assessment toolkit as part of our support to working-age people. Our use of this standardised assessment model means that our pre-employment support for blind and partially sighted people will be even more closely aligned to the specific needs of those we support.

Download (pdf 1.03 MB)

# Justin Macleod

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/justin-macleod/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

I have taught students in the areas of audio restoration; mixing; basic mastering, audio fundamentals and concepts; electronic music production; dialogue editing; and sound design. I offer a free consultation where prospective students and I can get a feel for one another and where I can find out what previous experience the student has and what their audio aspirations are so we can go over a possible lesson plan. I use this time to find out the student's preferred learning style as well.

My lessons include, where applicable and if the student wishes, recordings of the lessons; the setting and evaluation of exercises so that they can practice what they've learned between lessons; between lesson support in case they encounter any problems or have questions; and supplementary notes or audio demonstrations of concepts they would like reinforced or to explore further.

# Personaleyes

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/personaleyes/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

Davinder Kullar from Personaleyes offers tailored training, support and coaching to blind and partially sighted people on a range of technology, such as computers, smart phones, tablets through to smart speakers and everyday living solutions. This is done in a supportive manner to enable people to be effective with the tools they own and they offer them quality and value to their life.

Examples of accessibility training includes

• Screen readers such as Windows Narrator, NVDA and JAWS on desktop

• Voiceover iOS and talkback on Android for smart phones and tablets

• Low vision adaptations such as Magnification on desktops, smart phones and tablets

• Advice on everyday living devices and options on acquiring them, such as in home kitchen and other tasks.

Accessibility consultancy is offered on aspects from website user testing for access needs, assessing physical environments and low vision training to people that interact with blind and partially sighted individuals, such as professionals through to friends and families. This is to ensure the best interactions occur and people feel comfortable with the knowledge and skills for the situations, environments and tools they need access to.

Coaching is provided with my personal years of living with a health condition and utilising a range of knowledge and experience to provide a space to go through situations, options/ approaches and support the action to implement them. Coaching is aimed to develop the person to where they would like to be in life.

# Professional Vision Services

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/professional-vision-services/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

Professional Vision Services was incorporated in 1990 by Philippa Wisbey - Managing Director and owner, importing the Magnilink brand of video magnifiers and reading machines from Low Vision International (LVI) into the UK. We are one of the oldest companies within the Visual Impairment field today.

Professional Vision Services own a substantial amount of LVI and therefore are in the unique position in the UK of designing and manufacturing products for the visually impaired market. To name one; The Magnilink Student Addition - which won the prestigious education BETT award and is still the only visually impaired product to win this award. Other products such as the Magnilink ZIP evolved from customer consultations and their requests.

All products can be demonstrated free of charge on site throughout the UK by qualified experienced staff. We can offer full installation and training on all products.

Professional Vision Services has a vast experience of the Employment and Education marketplace and can create bespoke solutions for every situation.

# RNIB: Technology for Independent Learning

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/rnib-technology-for-independent-learning/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

The RNIB provide an overview of the role of technology in the development of a child or young person, the role of the QTVI (Qualified Teachers of children and young people with Vision Impairment), and provide information on some the mainstream and specialist solutions which are available.

The use of technology to access learning and the world beyond school is an area of specialist skills development as set out in the Curriculum Framework for Children and Young People with Vision Impairment (CFVI) so, while settings would facilitate, the expectation would be that a QTVI would lead on this.

# See My Skills: Breaking the cycle of unemployment for blind and partially sighted people

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/see-my-skills-breaking-the-cycle-of-unemployment-for-blind-and-partially-sighted-people/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

This report by The Vision Foundation sets out a roadmap to ensure that everyone, sighted or blind, has the chance to enjoy the independence, purpose and meaning that employment can bring.

“Blind and partially sighted people do the vast majority of the jobs that sighted people do. They might do them a little differently – using specialist technology or admin support – but they do them successfully ” says Dr Olivia Curno, Chief Executive, Vision Foundation. In my role I’ve worked alongside blind or partially sighted politicians, journalists, lawyers, presenters, teachers, fundraisers, professors, artists, authors, actors, bankers, CEOs, entrepreneurs and chefs. But these success stories are far too few. In fact, if you’re a blind adult of working age in the UK, there is only a 1 in 4 chance that you’re working. That means that over 300,000 blind and partially sighted people are currently excluded from the workplace.

The lack of understanding about visual impairment by employers and Jobcentre Plus staff are major barriers to employment. The research highlighted the importance of working with employers and service providers to educate them to overcome negative attitudes.

The research also highlighted the importance of individual assessments to identify the support required and bespoke programmes to enable their participation in the labour market. This might include, for example, support to develop key skills (such as mobility and orientation or computer skills), counselling to help in acceptance of their visual impairment or support to develop self- advocacy skills.

Published July 2021.

Download (pdf 1,010.83 KB)

## Contact

No contact details yet.

## Listed under

- [Read research and reports](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/research/)
- [Research](https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/kinds/#research)

# Sight & Sound Technology

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/sight-sound-technology/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

Sight and Sound Technology is an accredited training provider with resources across the UK and Ireland.

We are experts in supplying and supporting assistive technology – software and hardware – designed for use by those with sight loss, to help them in keep independence and help in their everyday lives, be that work, education, round the home or out and about.

We provide training in sessions of 1, 2 or 3 hour blocks, depending upon location and the individual’s requirement. We are considerate of pace and IT experience and tailor the sessions to fit the user, incorporating their everyday needs into the design of the sessions.

Some examples of the assistive technology we train on are:

- Computer software for the visually impaired such as JAWS, ZoomText, Fusion and Supernova

- Braille and Blindness technology such as Notetakers, Braille displays and Braille learning devices such as Mountbatten

- The latest technology for low vision such as OrCam, Envision glasses.

We are expert in training for any age, from School right up to those happily retired!

## Contact

- Website: [sightandsound.co.uk](https://www.sightandsound.co.uk)
- Email: [info@sightandsound.co.uk](mailto:info@sightandsound.co.uk)

# Sight Loss and Technology Briefing Report, 2024

Canonical page: https://tka.unremarkable.me/resources/directory/sight-loss-and-technology-briefing-report-2024/

> **Preview.** This is a private preview of a website being built for a real charity, under an invented name. Names, pictures and numbers on it are made up.

This briefing has been produced and published on behalf of the technology group of The Sight Loss Alliance, which TKA is part of. Sound Without Sight is a new non-profit initiative, aimed at supporting sight-impaired people in the fields of audio and music. We will showcase blind and partially sighted talent, highlight how accessibility barriers can be overcome, combine collective knowledge, and challenge stereotypes.

We will support the blind and partially sighted community to access:

- Audio production: recording, editing, mixing, etc.

- Music notation: reading and composing, obtaining accessible scores, screen access technologies, etc.

- Performance: instrumental, vocal, speech; individual or group; beginner or professional.
